text:
arik: Observed another oscillation during a Friday afternoon burst: autoscaler rapidly attached preemptible GPUs, allocator mixed SKUs for packing, we saw a wave of tenant evictions and then scale-downs. Ended up with ~4 eviction cycles in 12 minutes. Anybody have a lightweight stabilization pattern we can ship quickly?
clare: I saw the traces. The problem looks like two-fold: (1) autoscaler treats newly-joined preemptible nodes as full capacity immediately; (2) allocator will happily mix SKUs which amplifies eviction when preemptible disappears.
tony: Two ideas that are minimally invasive: confidence-weighted headroom + SKU-mix penalty. Confidence-weighted headroom = each node reports a small stability_score (0..1). admission multiplies node_capacity * stability_score * ramp_weight.
mira: What's ramp_weight?
tony: A short probation factor that ramps from initial_weight -> 1.0 over probe_window. Example: initial 0.3, window 45s. So effective contribution of a hot preemptible is low for the first minute.
clare: I'd add a tenant-level policy: prefer_stable_only or allow_preemptible. Default: prefer_stable_only for latency-SLO customers. That avoids silently routing critical traffic to shaky capacity.
arik: Agree on tenant opt-out. Also want an eviction_cooldown marker: when a tenant is evicted due to preemptible loss, set eviction_backoff TTL which prevents immediate reassign to preemptible for that tenant.
mira: Sketch config (YAML):
```yaml
stability_policy:
  preemptible:
    initial_weight: 0.3
    probe_window: 45s
    ramp_curve: linear
  mix_penalty:
    cross_sku_penalty: 0.6 # multiply score to prefer homogeneous allocations
tenant_flags:
  prefer_stable_only_key: prefer_stable_only
  eviction_backoff_sec: 120
```
tony: Implementation notes: allocator emits placement_hint {stability_score: float, sku_family: string, frag_score: float}. Keep the hint tiny — one float + sku label. admission uses stability_score and ramp math; autoscaler applies mix_penalty when considering candidate fills.
clare: Telemetry we must track: preemptible_join_event_ts, placement_hint_stability_histogram, eviction_backoff_hits, mix_penalty_rejections, tenant_eviction_churn_rate. Dashboards needed before rollout.
mira: Rollout plan: feature-flag gate the policy. Steps: 1) allocator emits placement_hint in staging, 2) admission applies ramp math in staging, 3) enable for a small canary tenant group in prod (non-latency SLO), 4) monitor churn + latency, 5) widen.
arik: One safety check: if >40% of candidate headroom is preemptible in a decision, emit an alert and fail-open to conservative counting. Add an override flag for cost-sensitive tenants.
tony: Edge case: very short spikes (< probe_window) — could lose useful capacity. Add allow_short_burst boolean per-tenant to accept low-weighted preemptible for short bursts. We'll need to simulate burst shapes to pick defaults.
clare: Also we should surface an operator metric: preemptible_effective_capacity_ratio so SRE can see how much of our working capacity is preemptible-weighted.
sre-bot: Note: created tracking issue https://go/redwood/tickets/PRD-8132 and added oncall annotation.
mira: Action items: 1) I will prototype a 10k-tenant sim to tune initial_weight/probe_window, 2) tony will add placement_hint to allocator, 3) clare will own tenant flag control-plane change + audit events, 4) arik will draft the RFC and rollout checklist.
arik: Please tag the RFC with the sim results and include expected dashboard panels and alert thresholds. Aim to keep defaults conservative (initial_weight 0.25, probe_window 60s, cross_sku_penalty 0.5).
tony: I'll open the allocator PR today and include a small compatibility shim so older operators ignore the hint if absent.
mira: I'll wire dashboards and a canary cohort. Let's reconvene after the RFC PR lands. :thumbsup:
